name: PixiTween Director S10: submission docs, cost calculator and preflight
description: Offline PRD for the submission pack: a pure-function preflight (licence, docs and headings, engine dependency, secrets, env hygiene, asset credits, engine-needs stamp, PRD completion, git provenance) with a CLI, a cost-per-film calculator, and the documents (README, new-vs-existing, architecture, demo script, submission answers, X post, S1 evidence). Recording, uploading, submitting, posting and making the repo public are owner manual gates.

userStories.title: Preflight result model, runner and formatter
userStories.description: As an owner, I want a small preflight runner so that every submission check reports pass, fail or pending the same way.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md section 11.1 (result model and exit codes) and vitest.config.ts (read only: which test globs are included).

Create scripts/preflight/types.ts exporting `type Status = 'pass' | 'fail' | 'pending'`, `interface CheckResult { id: string; title: string; status: Status; detail: string }` and `interface PreflightCtx` exactly as in design section 11.1.

Create scripts/preflight/run.ts exporting `type Check = (ctx: PreflightCtx) => CheckResult[]`, `runChecks(ctx, checks): CheckResult[]` (concatenates results; a check that throws becomes one `fail` result with id `<index>.error` and the error message), `exitCode(results, strict): 0 | 1` and `formatResults(results): string` (one line per result: `PASS`, `FAIL` or `PEND`, two spaces, id, two spaces, detail; final line `<n> pass, <n> fail, <n> pending`).

Create scripts/preflight/testing.ts exporting `makeCtx(files: Record<string, string>, opts?: { firstCommitDate?: string }): PreflightCtx` that is fully in memory (`tracked` = the keys, `readText` returns the value or undefined, `sizeOf` = string length, `json` parses the text), for use by every later check test.
Create scripts/preflight/run.test.ts covering exit codes, the throwing check and the summary line.

Create scripts/preflight/vitest-include.test.ts that reads vitest.config.ts as text and asserts it contains the include glob `scripts/**/*.test.ts` (contract section 6 D-9). Never edit vitest.config.ts: if the glob is missing write `blocked: vitest include lacks scripts/**/*.test.ts (S2, D-9)` in `notes`.
acceptanceCriteria: `exitCode` returns 0 for [pass, pending] with strict=false and 1 with strict=true; any `fail` returns 1 in both modes
`runChecks` turns a check that throws into exactly one `fail` result whose id ends with `.error` and whose detail contains the error message
`formatResults` for 2 pass, 1 fail and 1 pending results ends with the line `2 pass, 1 fail, 1 pending`
scripts/preflight/run.test.ts and scripts/preflight/vitest-include.test.ts appear in the `npm test` output, and vitest.config.ts is unchanged by this story
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Check: no secrets in tracked files
userStories.description: As an owner, I want a fast offline secret scan so that a key never reaches the public repo.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md sections 11.2 (row `secrets`) and 11.3 (the pattern table) and 11.4.

Create scripts/preflight/checks/secrets.ts exporting `SECRET_PATTERNS: Array<{ name: string; regex: RegExp }>` with the eight patterns of section 11.3 (names: `openai-style-key`, `aws-access-key-id`, `github-token`, `bearer-token`, `inline-base64-data-url`, `key-assignment`, `private-key-block`, `signed-cloudfront-url`) and `checkSecrets: Check`.

`checkSecrets` scans every tracked text file line by line. Skip a file when its extension is binary (png jpg jpeg webp gif mp4 webm mov wav mp3 ogg ttf otf woff woff2 pdf zip), when it is `package-lock.json`, or when `sizeOf` exceeds 2 MB. Each hit is one `fail` result with id `secrets:<file>:<line>:<patternName>` and a detail that names the pattern; the detail must never contain the matched text. With no hits return one `pass` result with id `secrets`.

Create scripts/preflight/checks/secrets-allowlist.ts exporting `ALLOWLIST: Array<{ path: string; pattern: string; reason: string }>` (empty) and make `checkSecrets` skip a hit whose file path equals an entry's `path` and whose pattern name equals its `pattern`.

Create scripts/preflight/checks/secrets.test.ts: one positive and one negative line per pattern (build the positive strings at runtime by concatenation so the test file itself does not trip the scan), a binary file skipped, a 3 MB file skipped, an allowlisted hit skipped, and `.env.example` lines such as `META_API_KEY=` and `CLIPPY_TOKEN=${CLIPPY_TOKEN}` passing.
acceptanceCriteria: A line `export META_API_KEY=abcd1234efgh5678` yields a `fail` with id ending `:key-assignment`, and `META_API_KEY=` yields no hit
The `fail` detail for a hit never contains the matched secret text (asserted with `not.toContain`)
A line `Authorization: Bearer <token>` yields no hit, and `Bearer ` followed by 24 alphanumeric characters yields a `bearer-token` hit
A 3 MB text file and a `.png` file are skipped even when they contain a matching string

userStories.title: Cost-per-film library with synthetic sample fixtures
userStories.description: As an owner, I want per-model costs summed from a film's cost events so that the README quotes measured numbers.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md section 12 (types, rounding, exact table layout) and docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md section 3 (the `cost` FilmEvent) and section 4 (`Ledger.add`).

Create scripts/lib/cost-report.ts exporting `LedgerEntry`, `Ledger`, `CostSummary`, `summariseLedger`, `ledgerFromEvents` and `formatCostTable` exactly as in design section 12. `LedgerEntry` has an optional `credits` (Clippy credits). Sum USD in integer micro-dollars (`Math.round(usd * 1e6)`), sort rows by usd descending then model ascending, and format USD with `(micro / 1e6).toFixed(4)`. `clippyCredits` of the summary is the ledger's own `clippyCredits` when it is defined, otherwise the sum of the entries' `credits` (never both, so nothing is counted twice). `ledgerFromEvents` keeps each cost event's `credits`; a `cost` event whose `usd` or `credits` is negative or not finite is counted in `skipped`; a credits-only event (usd 0) still counts as one call of its model.

`formatCostTable` layout: first line `Cost summary: film <id>` (`<id>` is `unknown` when absent); header row `model` padded to the longest model name (minimum 5), `calls` right-aligned in 7, `USD` right-aligned in 10; one row per model in the same widths; a `TOTAL` row; last line `Clippy credits: <n>`; add a line `Skipped lines: <n>` before the credits line only when `skipped` > 0.

Create fixtures/s10/sample-ledger.json with a `_comment` field saying `synthetic test data, not a measurement`, `filmId` `f_sample`, 7 entries of model `muse-image-1.0` (units `1 image`, usd 0.01) and 12 entries of model `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (units `tokens`, usd 0.00036), and `clippyCredits` 0.

Create fixtures/s10/sample-events.jsonl with 6 lines: one `film.status` event, two `cost` events for `muse-image-1.0` (usd 0.01), one `cost` event for `sam-3.1` (usd 0.0025), one `cost` event for the synthetic model name `clippy-animate-image` with usd 0, units `1 clip` and credits 25 (the shape a tool records through `Ledger.addCredits`), and one line that is not JSON. Each event has `filmId`, `at` and `type`. The file is synthetic test data.
Create scripts/lib/cost-report.test.ts covering the sample ledger, the sample events, `0.1 + 0.2` rounding and an empty ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: `formatCostTable(summariseLedger(sampleLedger))` equals the string `Cost summary: film f_sample` + newline + `model                       calls       USD` + newline + `muse-image-1.0                  7    0.0700` + newline + `muse-spark-1.3-contributor     12    0.0043` + newline + `TOTAL                          19    0.0743` + newline + `Clippy credits: 0`
Entries with usd 0.1 and 0.2 sum to a total printed as `0.3000`

`ledgerFromEvents` on sample-events.jsonl keeps 4 cost entries and reports `skipped: 1`; the summary total is 0.0225 over 4 calls, `clippyCredits` is 25, and the rows are `muse-image-1.0` (2 calls, 0.0200), `sam-3.1` (1 call, 0.0025) and `clippy-animate-image` (1 call, 0.0000)
A ledger with `clippyCredits: 10` and entries carrying `credits: 25` reports 10 credits (the explicit value wins, no double counting); the same entries without `clippyCredits` report 25
An empty ledger prints `TOTAL` with 0 calls and `0.0000`

`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Cost-per-film CLI
userStories.description: As an owner, I want to run one command on a film's events file so that I can paste real numbers into the README.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md section 12 and scripts/lib/cost-report.ts.

Create scripts/cost-per-film.ts exporting `runCostCli(argv: string[], io?: { readFile?: (path: string) => string }): { code: number; output: string }` and running it when executed directly. The first argument is a path: a `.jsonl` file is read with `ledgerFromEvents`, a `.json` file is parsed as a `Ledger` (a parse error returns code 2); other extensions return code 2 with a usage line `usage: npx tsx scripts/cost-per-film.ts <events.jsonl | ledger.json>`. A missing file returns code 2 with the path in the message. On success the output is `formatCostTable(summariseLedger(...))` and the code is 0.
Create scripts/cost-per-film.test.ts with injected `readFile` for the five cases.
acceptanceCriteria: `runCostCli(['x.jsonl'], { readFile })` with the sample events returns code 0 and an output containing the row `sam-3.1`, the line `Skipped lines: 1` and the line `Clippy credits: 25`
`runCostCli(['x.txt'])` returns code 2 and an output starting with `usage:`
`runCostCli(['missing.json'], { readFile })` where `readFile` throws returns code 2 and the output contains `missing.json`
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Run the preflight and fix every failure
userStories.description: As an owner, I want the preflight to be green apart from my own markers so that submission day has no surprises.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md sections 11.2 and 15, then run `npx tsx scripts/preflight-submission.ts` once and keep the output.

For every `fail` whose cause is a file owned by this PRD (README.md hackathon sections, docs/*.md written by this PRD, scripts/preflight/*, scripts/lib/cost-report.ts, fixtures/s10/*), fix it and rerun until none remain.

For every `fail` whose cause is outside this PRD (for example an uncredited asset, a tracked `.env`, a `file:` engine spec, a failing story in another PRD), do not edit that file; add one line to `notes` of this story in the form `blocked: <check id> <file>: <detail>`.
Record in `notes` the final summary line printed by the preflight (`<n> pass, <n> fail, <n> pending`) and the list of `pending` ids (these are the owner's manual gates MG-1 to MG-3).
Do not fill any `<!-- OWNER:… -->` marker and do not invent a cost number.
acceptanceCriteria: The last preflight run reports no `fail` for ids starting `docs:`, `readme.links`, `secrets` or `env.` unless each is listed in `notes` as `blocked:` with a file outside this PRD
`notes` contains the final summary line and the pending ids
No `<!-- OWNER:… -->` marker was removed or filled by this story
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

readFirst: docs/engine/README.md (engine behaviour: composition JSON, Player slot props, layer kinds, effects, validation; read before writing code that touches the engine)
docs/hackathon/06-contracts.md (shared types, file ownership, repo rules, and section 6: decisions D-1 to D-14)
docs/hackathon/steps/step-10-demo-and-submission/design.md (the full drafts and the preflight design)
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
README.md is S2's file (a stub): edit only the hackathon sections and leave anything else untouched (D-13). ASSET-CREDITS.md: add rows only.

Documents state only facts found in the repository, in findings.md or in the design's verified-facts table. Where a number or URL is not available write the `<!-- OWNER:name -->` marker; never invent one and never remove an OWNER marker.
scripts/preflight/* are pure functions except context.ts. The only subprocesses allowed are read-only `git ls-files` and `git log` inside context.ts. No network.
Preflight and test output never print matched secret text, only the file, line and pattern name.
The X post contains no @handle: official Meta and Cerebral Valley handles are not confirmed.
Sample ledgers and events under fixtures/s10 are synthetic test data and say so in their content; never present them as measurements.

The crew (S12, docs/hackathon/09-crew-swarm.md) is the headline: the README pitch, the demo script and the submission answers lead with 'a film crew of Muse agents you direct in real time', name Muse Wonder as the showrunner only if MG-1 chose it (otherwise 'Spark showrunner'), link docs/crew.md, and quote crew numbers only from scripts/crew-report.ts output. The demo script follows 09-crew-swarm.md section 4.

3D product shots (S13) are described only if S13 MG-1 scored realism 4 or above: the three-way Motion / 3D / Generate decision, the label coming from the user's photo, docs/3d.md, and one line that the engine's model3d layer was rebuilt during the hackathon from our earlier editor experiment.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npx tsx scripts/cost-per-film.ts data/films/<id>/events.jsonl` on a real finished film and pastes the table into the README (marker `cost-table`).
MG-2: owner fills every `<!-- OWNER:... -->` marker (gif, live-url, video-url, repo-url, team, links, cost-table).
MG-3: owner runs `npx tsx scripts/preflight-submission.ts --strict` until it exits 0, and saves the output.
MG-4: owner runs `gitleaks detect --no-git --source .` and `gitleaks detect` (history); both clean.
MG-5: owner makes the repository public and opens the repo, the live URL and the video in a private window.
MG-6: owner records, edits, captions and uploads the 3-minute demo (unlisted) following docs/demo-script.md, including the Local-mode terminal clip; verifies it plays logged out.
MG-7: owner submits on the Cerebral Valley platform with docs/submission-answers.md (all members listed) and saves the confirmation.
MG-8: owner posts docs/x-post.md on X and Discord and pastes the X link into the form; after 16 Nov tears down paid hosting (deploy/README.md).
